transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ethan, Sara (Redwood) - Jared, Priya, Marco, Lena (Ventra)

Summary:
Quick weekly checkpoint on the Ventra KV/priming POC. Focus on priming thresholds, observed hit-rate delta across checkout/support flows, and the cold-start tail. Agreement to share experiment CSVs and run two narrowly scoped slices this week.

Topics:
- Observed KV hit-rate trends (global vs per-route)
- Prompt reuse pattern anomalies during peak orders
- Eviction/priming thresholds and cost vs latency tradeoffs
- Next benchmarks and infra access

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Brooks: hey everyone thanks for joining on time appreciate it, we are on the weekly Ventra priming checkpoint. quick round robin?
[00:12] Jared Cole: hey Jared here, quick context we ran the updated priming with the 3-tier threshold last night, saw some improvements but there are weird drops at the 21:00 UTC window.
[00:24] Priya Nair: priya — product — and we want to understand whether the hit-rate change was real or noise from the migration.
[00:31] Sara Li: Sara from Redwood, i'll pull up the metrics i have and explain the small tweak we made to kv expiry, it was basically changing the reuse-window for session tokens from 120s to 45s for the checkout path.
[00:45] Marco Ruiz: Marco — infra — i pushed the new autoscaler rule same time, could be confounding the results.
[00:52] Ethan Brooks: ok, so agenda, 1) quick numbers 2) dig into checkout vs support chat 3) decide on the two slices to run, 4) next steps. sound good?
[01:04] Group: yes / yep / mmhmm
[01:10] Sara Li: alright, numbers first — global kv hit-rate improved from 28% to 37% after our priming patch, but checkout hit-rate only moved from 15% to 19%. support chat went from 42% to 60% which is a big win.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: that matches what we saw in product — support messages have more reuse prefixes, checkout uses a lot of ephemeral tokens per transaction so reuse is lower.
[01:42] Jared Cole: the weird part is at 21:00 UTC the checkout hit-rate dips to 7% for a ten minute window. logs show a spike in new session IDs. maybe a mobile release?
[01:58] Priya Nair: yes there was a client patch at 20:56 that introduced a short-lived session handshake. we should correlate with release timeline.
[02:10] Sara Li: that explains new session IDs; priming helps when there is prefix overlap — if session ids change every request we won't get reuse. our recommendation is to split checkout into two sub-routes: 'checkout-cart' and 'checkout-confirm' and only prime cart where reuse is heavier.
[02:30] Ethan Brooks: good, that is a low-effort routing change. Marco, is it easy to tag those routes at the edge?
[02:37] Marco Ruiz: yes we can add a header X-Ventra-Route: cart|confirm, we have a quick deploy, i can do that tomorrow.
[02:45] Sara Li: perfect. also we noticed KV key cardinality exploded because some fields included ephemeral request IDs; we suggested normalizing the key by hashing and truncating the user-agent chunk. that will reduce noise.
[02:58] Lena Ortiz: do you have an example normalization rule?
[03:03] Sara Li: yes — we'll send a snippet. basically strip timestamps, keep browser family, hash the rest to 8 chars. it'll be in the shared doc.
[03:12] Jared Cole: about eviction, we tried a size-based LRU but the checkout path saw eviction storms. Sara any changes?
[03:20] Sara Li: we recommend a hybrid: sticky-per-session for cart keys with TTL 8 minutes and adaptive LRU for the rest with a soft-evict threshold that scales based on recent hit-rate. this reduces simultaneous evictions during peaks.
[03:39] Ethan Brooks: can you explain soft-evict threshold in simple terms?
[03:44] Sara Li: yeah — instead of hard evicting when memory hits X, we lower the threshold gradually when observed hit-rate falls below target. it's kind of like thermostatic eviction, gives the cache time to warm.
[03:58] Priya Nair: curious about cost — will sticky-per-session blow up memory?
[04:04] Sara Li: it's targeted — only for cart keys which are a small portion of total keys. estimated memory bump ~6% but hit-rate uplift in cart estimated to be 2.5x, so net token cost drops. we'll share the numbers.
[04:19] Marco Ruiz: note — our GPU nodes are also doing other workloads; can't increase memory without approval. we'll rely on tuned TTLs.
[04:28] Ethan Brooks: ok noted. next, cold-start tail — we saw 95th percentile cold-start generation latency spike to 1.2s for newly primed sessions. thoughts?
[04:39] Sara Li: that's expected when you prime long KV chains. we can do lazy priming where we only materialize the top-2 most probable prefixes synchronously and background the rest. that shaves tail latency by ~300ms in our lab.
[04:56] Lena Ortiz: background priming needs idempotency; are there race conditions?
[05:01] Sara Li: there can be but we use monotonic write tokens and de-dup keys at write time; we'll share the pattern.
[05:10] Jared Cole: another ask — can we get a per-route heatmap of prefix lengths and their reuse frequency? that would help pick thresholds per-route.
[05:19] Ethan Brooks: yes, Sara can produce that from the telemetry.
[05:23] Sara Li: i'll export a heatmap CSV for checkout-cart, checkout-confirm, and supportchat — expect it in the shared folder by monday.
[05:33] Priya Nair: for the two test slices you mentioned, what are you proposing?
[05:38] Sara Li: slice A = checkout-cart only with sticky-per-session enabled and hash normalization; slice B = support chat baseline (control) but with slightly tighter TTLs to compare cost. run for 48 hours.
[05:50] Marco Ruiz: we can route 10% of checkout traffic to slice A and keep the rest unchanged. will need a quick edge rule rollout.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: we'll annotate expected key reuse in the test plan.
[06:03] Ethan Brooks: schedule wise — Sara to share statements and config by 2026-09-06; Marco to roll edge header on 09-04; Ventra to run slices 09-06 to 09-08; deep-dive benchmark scheduled 09-08.
[06:20] Jared Cole: a note on anomalies — on the 21:00 dip we saw a correlated autoscaler short spike; if autoscaler replaced nodes, cache lost warm state. can Redwood suggest fallback policies?
[06:33] Sara Li: yes — we have a regional soft-routing fallback that routes low-priority traffic to a cheaper but warmer pool; also an edge-side prefetch to the new node during scale-up. both are somewhat infra heavy, but we can prototype.
[06:49] Marco Ruiz: prototype time window 2 weeks? we can prioritize after slice results.
[06:55] Priya Nair: one compliance question — does priming materialize any PII? our support chat contains small snippets of PII in transcripts.
[07:03] Sara Li: priming keys are hashed and we avoid storing raw transcripts in the cache; Redwood's default is KMS-encrypted cache at-rest and we can give audit logs for access. we'll attach security note.
[07:16] Ethan Brooks: ok good. Competitors pop-up — Jared asked if we should consider Anthropic for the checkout baseline because of lower tokenization overhead? is that being considered?
[07:27] Jared Cole: yeah just exploring options; cost model still favors Redwood given priming gains.
[07:33] Ethan Brooks: thanks. any final questions?
[07:36] Priya Nair: quick ask — can you include a minimal curl example to set the X-Ventra-Route header for the test?
[07:42] Sara Li: yes i'll add one to the doc.
[07:45] Marco Ruiz: i'll follow up with infra access once i grant the bucket role. expect a note by end of day.
[07:51] Ethan Brooks: recap — action items we listed, next steps dates, schedule deep-dive for 09-08. thanks everyone.
[07:58] Group: thanks / bye

Notes: transcript has minor speaker attribution noise, some technical terms spelled phonetically (kv vs k-v), and occasional filler words. Shared artifacts referenced: link to hit-rate spreadsheet (S3 link placeholder), priming config snippet (doc link), security checklist (doc link).
